title: Cjarsons della Carnia
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A remarkable stuffed pasta from the Carnia mountains combining sweet and savory in one filling — potato, herbs, raisins, cinnamon, and cocoa — finished with melted butter, smoked ricotta, and sugar.
longDesc: Cjarsons is one of the most unusual pasta fillings in all of Italy, its combination of savory potato and herbs with raisins, chocolate, and cinnamon reflecting the mountainous Carnia area's isolation and its own distinct culinary evolution.
ingredients: 300 g (10.5 oz) potatoes, boiled and mashed
50 g (⅓ cup) raisins, soaked and chopped
steps: Combine the flour, eggs, water, and salt into a smooth dough, kneading until elastic. Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the mashed potato with the raisins, grated chocolate, cinnamon, mint, and marjoram into a well-mixed filling.
Roll the pasta dough thin and cut into rounds using a cutter, about 8cm across.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each round and fold in half, pressing the edges firmly to seal into a half-moon shape.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the cjarsons for 3–4 minutes until they float.
Meanwhile, melt the butter until lightly browned and fragrant.
Drain the pasta and toss gently in the browned butter.
Serve immediately, topped with grated smoked ricotta and a light dusting of sugar.
chefTips: This filling is genuinely meant to taste both sweet and savory at once — don't be tempted to reduce the sugar or chocolate.
Seal the edges firmly, as the potato filling can be somewhat loose and prone to leaking if not sealed well.
The final touch of sugar over the savory smoked ricotta is traditional and part of what makes this dish so distinctive.
commonMistakes: Being hesitant about the sweet-savory combination and reducing the sugar or spice, which loses the dish's authentic character.
Overfilling the pasta, making it difficult to seal properly.
Skipping the smoked ricotta topping, which provides an essential contrast to the sweeter elements.
servedWith: A light white wine from Friuli
storage: Fresh, uncooked cjarsons can be frozen for up to 1 month.
reheating: Best cooked fresh; do not reheat already-cooked pasta.
healthBenefits: Potato provides carbohydrates for energy, with modest amounts of protein from the cheese and eggs.
culturalNote: Cjarsons hails from the remote Carnia mountains of Friuli, its unusual sweet-savory profile a testament to the area's isolated history and distinct culinary evolution separate from the rest of Italy.
